title: One step of the leftward seek
statement: Let $W$ be a finite binary Turing machine, let $a,R\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be an input word over the schedule alphabet, and let $u,g\in\mathbb{Z}$. For a base configuration of the schedule machine on $x$, suppose its guide tape is the fixed guide of radius $R$. From the leftward-seek phase with guide head at $g$, one step enters the forward phase and moves the guide head to $g+1$ if $g=-R-1$; otherwise it remains in the leftward-seek phase and moves the guide head to $g-1$.
hypotheses_covered: $W$ is a finite binary Turing machine
$x$ is an input word over the schedule alphabet
the base guide tape is the fixed guide of radius $R$
replaced:
Suppose the base's guide tape is the fixed guide of radius $R$.  From the
leftward-seek phase with guide head at $g$, one step of the schedule controller turns
into the forward phase and moves the guide head right exactly when $g = -R - 1$, and
otherwise stays in the seek phase and moves the guide head left.
